headline: A cool, dry weekend for coastal San Diego County gives way to a chance of light showers Sunday night into Monday morning, while rising King Tides bring a Coastal Flood Advisory starting Sunday morning and a Coastal Flood Watch through Thursday afternoon.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: The storm that moved through Thursday keeps heading east, so Friday afternoon is dry, with clouds clearing from the coast to the foothills into the evening. Temperatures away from the coast run 5 to 10 degrees below normal. Tonight, north and east winds are breeziest along the coastal mountain slopes, with gusts mostly under 35 mph; west winds gusting about 30–35 mph through mountain passes into the deserts ease by about 3 PM.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday and Sunday stay dry with light breezes from the land, and areas away from the coast stay 5 to 10 degrees below normal, with chilly mornings in the 30s in parts of the Inland Empire, below freezing in the high desert and in the teens around Big Bear Lake. A small piece of a larger Pacific Northwest storm brings a chance of light rain Sunday evening and night everywhere except the lower deserts, and showers may linger into Monday morning in southern San Diego County, including the metro area. Rain should total around a tenth of an inch, locally more in the mountains; with snow levels near 5,000 feet, San Bernardino Mountain communities have the best chance of accumulating snow, generally under an inch at places like Big Bear Lake.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Tuesday stays cool and dry. Another storm approaches the Pacific Northwest early in the week, and it is unclear whether a piece of it breaks off and reaches Southern California or high pressure to the south keeps it to the north; if it arrives, light showers are possible closer to the coast sometime Wednesday into Thanksgiving morning. Otherwise, high pressure strengthens through the middle and end of the week, bringing drier weather and a warming trend with highs 5 to 10 degrees above normal.

coast: Morning high tides keep climbing, topping 7 feet by Sunday, and King Tides peak Wednesday, with morning high tides of 7.9–8.2 feet Tuesday through Thursday (forecasters nudged the tide forecast above the usual predictions based on recent observations). A Coastal Flood Advisory covers the Orange County and San Diego County coasts from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM Tuesday, followed by a Coastal Flood Watch from late Monday night through Thursday afternoon. Surf stays around 3–5 feet through Wednesday, but a new swell arriving Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf starting Thursday, on top of the high tides. Offshore, gusts around 30–35 mph and choppy, locally steep 6–8 foot seas continue in the outer waters under a Small Craft Advisory until 9 PM Friday for waters 10 to 60 nautical miles out from San Mateo Point to the Mexican border, including San Clemente Island; no further marine hazards are expected through Tuesday, but the midweek storm and swell could bring hazardous winds and waves back Wednesday into Thursday.
watch_for: King Tides: Coastal Flood Advisory Sunday to Tuesday morning, then a Coastal Flood Watch through Thursday afternoon, with morning tides near 8 feet and possibly bigger surf Thursday.
Light rain Sunday night into Monday morning (about a tenth of an inch) and light mountain snow above about 5,000 feet.
Whether the midweek system reaches the area with light coastal showers Wednesday into Thanksgiving morning.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the dry, cool weekend and note rain chances for Sunday night have ticked up slightly, but whether the midweek system reaches Southern California remains uncertain.
